title: KV: sparse fragment index and delta evictor to reduce spill noise and lower memory churn
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Under mixed traffic we observed frequent small spillouts from the KV cache that caused background paging thrash and extra allocator churn. Root cause analysis showed fragmentation hotspots where many small freed segments prevented contiguous reservation for critical prefetched pages. This PR introduces a sparse fragment index (SFI) and a delta-based evictor that cooperates with the scheduler to make eviction decisions on coarse-grained deltas rather than per-page heuristics. The goal is to reduce spill frequency, reduce allocator fragmentation, and smooth background IO without increasing tail latency.

What this changes (high level):
- New in-memory sparse fragment index (kv/sfi) that tracks free-run metadata per-extent and gives a compact view of fragmentation hotspots per-tenant. The index exposes occupancy histograms and contiguous-run estimators used by the eviction policy.
- Delta Evictor: a policy layer that consumes SFI signals and computes eviction plans as deltas (byte ranges / extents) to minimize the number of evict operations and to preserve larger contiguous blocks. The evictor prefers soft-preemption (move-to-staging) to full spill when possible.
- Scheduler hooks: serving runtime scheduler now takes an "eviction-cost" penalty into request placement decisions to avoid scheduling heavy prefetches at memory pressure peaks. Small integration: scheduler/eager-preempt path uses SFI occupancy to avoid eviction storms.
- A metric bridge and tracing: new metrics kv.sfi.fragmentation_score, kv.evictor.delta_ops, kv.evictor.avg_eviction_size, and traces for eviction decisions to aid post-deploy validation.

Design notes: The SFI is intentionally approximate to keep memory and compute overheads low (bitmap + summarized extents per shard). It shards by tenant and by allocator-bucket. The delta evictor batches eviction intents produced during a scheduling window (configurable default 50ms) and emits a single coalesced operation to the pager when appropriate. This reduces IOPs and amortizes KV indexing costs.

Benchmarks (local perf lab w/ realistic tenant mix):
- 95th-percentile spill events per-minute: down from 18.4 -> 6.1 (66% reduction)
- Background IO throughput (bytes/sec for spill writes): down ~48% at 95th workload
- Median eviction op size: increased from 4KB -> 48KB (better coalescing)
- P50 generation latency (hosted inference light queries): unchanged (+0.3ms noise), P99 latency increased by +0.8ms under synthetic adversarial prefetch tests (within SLO).
- Memory fragmentation score (kv.sfi.fragmentation_score, lower is better): median 0.32 -> 0.12 across tenants tested.

Testing: Unit tests cover SFI update/merge and eviction heuristics (edge cases: repeated small frees, long-running contiguous reservations). Integration tests run in perf-canary with a mixed-tenancy replay trace. A new end-to-end stress (kv-ejector-stress) replicates the previous incident profile and validates that spill counts remain bounded. CI had a flaky integration test which was isolated and retried (see CI notes).

Backward compatibility & rollout: The SFI and delta evictor are gated behind a runtime feature flag (kv.sfi.enabled=false by default). Rollout plan: enable in perf-canary, monitor kv.* metrics for 48h, then staged rollout to Dedicated fleets with gradual tenant ramp. A rollback path exists to disable the feature flag and trigger immediate revert of pending eviction windows.

Risks / mitigations:
- Risk: coalescing could delay hot-item eviction and affect tail latency. Mitigation: delta evictor has a max-latency budget per window and falls back to immediate per-page eviction if budget is exceeded.
- Risk: SFI memory overhead. Mitigation: index is budgeted per-tenant and sampled; default config limits memory to ~1% of tenant cache; can be tuned or disabled.

Related work: follow-ups planned to integrate SFI hints into the prefix/KV cache prefetcher and to expose compacted extent lists to the on-disk pager for smarter writeback ordering. See Linear ENG-1892 and ENG-2041 for follow-up items.

Checklist: Implemented, unit tests, integration tests, perf numbers attached, rollout plan and rollback documented in the PR description.

Notes: This PR avoids touching the allocator internals; it composes with the existing slab allocator and slot coalescer by providing eviction intents rather than making in-place heap changes. That design tradeoff simplifies rollback and reduces cross-team coordination risk.
